shariahReviewStatus.statement: Every Shariah-bearing field, rule and standard reference in this fragment was modelled by an engineer from the research record. None has been reviewed by a Shariah supervisory board. No standard clause number is cited anywhere, because none was read; bodies, standard numbers and titles are cited and marked clauseVerified:false. Until a named SSB signs off, this is a reference implementation and the README must say so (DESIGN.md section 9).
shariahReviewStatus.citationDiscipline: AAOIFI/IFSB/OIC/BNM references name the body, the standard and its subject only. Where I could not cite a standard I said so in the domain's shariah.uncertain rather than supplying a plausible number.

typeVocabulary.note: CLOSED. A field type outside this table cannot be generated and must not be added to a catalog entry without adding it here first - that is what keeps 48 domains on ONE template. Each row is the complete mechanical mapping.

ratio.openapi: {type: object, required: [numerator, denominator], properties: {numerator: int64, denominator: int64}}

quantity.note: integer quantity in the stated unit. Fractional quantities are expressed by choosing a smaller unit, never by a float.

typeVocabulary.moneyRule: every moneyMinor field is a signed int64 count of minor units, names a currencyField, and has its ISO 4217 exponent looked up in the generated currency table. No float, no decimal string, no percentage field anywhere in this fragment. Division appears only as floorDiv.
typeVocabulary.ratioRule: ProfitSharingRatio and every other share is the 'ratio' type: two int64 columns and exact integer cross-multiplication. There is no float share in this fragment and no percentage column.

ruleExpressionGrammar.note: A prose assert cannot be compiled. Every assert below is in this closed grammar so ONE rules-component template can emit a real predicate plus a generated test. Anything that does not fit the grammar is reported as a gap, not written as prose.

functions.sum(bq[].field): integer sum over a behaviour-qualifier collection
functions.floorDiv(a, b): exact integer division, rounds toward negative infinity; the ONLY division permitted in a money path
functions.ratioSum(r1, r2, ...): exact ratio addition by integer cross-multiplication; compares to 1 without ever producing a float
functions.unchanged(field): the UPDATE does not alter this column (compares the prior row; the repository already reads it for the optimistic-lock version)
functions.hasField(regex): GENERATE-TIME only: does any field of this control record or BQ match the regex
functions.stageAtLeast(stage): the record has reached that point in its declared stage enum order

appliesTo.bq.<Name>.write: POST/PUT on the generated sub-resource for that behaviour qualifier
appliesTo.generate: evaluated by the generator against the catalog entry itself; a violation FAILS THE BUILD and stamps nothing

onViolation.reject: HTTP 422 with the rule's code as an RFC 9457 problem type; nothing is persisted
onViolation.flag: the write succeeds AND an append-only shariah_finding row plus a shariah.compliance.flagged event are written (DESIGN.md 5.8). A flag is never silent.

ruleExpressionGrammar.hasFieldContract: hasField(regex) matches the field's SNAKE_CASE column name, not its camelCase name, and every alternative is anchored with (^|_)...(_|$). This is not cosmetic: an unanchored 'apr' matches 'aPr' inside totalIstisnaPriceMinor and would have failed the Istisna build on a perfectly valid schema. The generator asserts that no generate-time regex matches a legitimate field in its own domain, so a banned-token list can never be widened into a false positive unnoticed. Each list is scoped to ITS OWN entry and must never be hoisted into the shared template: Qard Hassan bans 'profit' outright, which would be wrong for Musharakah.

roundingPolicy.rule: every proportional split is floorDiv on the first party and the arithmetic RESIDUAL on the second, so the parts always sum exactly to the whole and no minor unit is created or lost.

whoTakesTheResidual.Mudarabah Venture Financing: mudarib floored, rabb-ul-mal takes the residual
whoTakesTheResidual.Diminishing Musharakah Home Finance: bank floored, customer takes the residual; rent floors in the customer's favour
whoTakesTheResidual.Musharakah Partnership Financing: each partner floored, largest capital holder absorbs the residual

roundingPolicy.honesty: the residual direction is an ENGINEERING choice I made for conservation, not a Shariah ruling. A board may require a different direction or a periodic true-up. Each domain repeats this in shariah.uncertain.

areaNotes.domainListSource: read from catalog/islamic-service-landscape.json. The orchestrator's area guidance named 11 domains and omitted 'Asset Acquisition Agency'; it is in the catalog and is included, because it is the domain that decides whether every Murabaha in the area is structurally honest.
areaNotes.structuralIntegrity: the sale/lease/partnership mechanics are modelled so the difference is machine-checkable, not narrative: a sale carries an ownership timestamp with evidence and an amount with no rate (ISB-MRB-02, ISB-MRB-12); a lease carries ownership risk that cannot be shifted and rent that stops when usufruct stops (ISB-IJR-02/03/04); a partnership carries profit by agreed exact ratio and loss strictly by capital share (ISB-MSH-01/02/03, ISB-MDB-01/02/03); a benevolent loan repays exactly what it lent (ISB-QRD-01).
areaNotes.noRateFields: there is no interest rate, APR, profit rate, benchmark rate, penalty rate or percentage field in any of the 12 entries. Eleven generate-time hasField assertions fail the build if one is ever added.
areaNotes.lateChargesNeverIncome: nine domains declare a Late Payment Charge BQ whose destination enum is checked against CharityPool; the gharamahDestination enum in Late Payment Charity Handling has exactly ONE value, and ISB-LPC-03 additionally checks the GL account class, so the claim is provable from the ledger rather than from the application's intent.
areaNotes.coinedBQs: a behaviourQualifier with bianBQ:null has no BIAN counterpart and is marked so in its note. BIAN's loan and lease domains have no asset-purchase leg, no usufruct interruption and no charity destination, because a conventional loan needs none of them. Where a real BIAN BQ fits (Repayment, Disbursement, Collateral, Asset, Fee, Insurance, Maintenance, Valuation, Payment Schedule, Assessment) it is used by name.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Asset Acquisition
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined: BIAN's loan SDs have no purchase leg because a conventional loan never buys anything. This BQ is the structural difference and the first thing an auditor asks for.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Disbursement
behaviourQualifiers.note: money goes to the SUPPLIER, not to the customer. A disbursement to the customer is the single clearest sign the asset leg is fictional (ISB-MRB-09).

behaviourQualifiers.name: Late Payment Charge

behaviourQualifiers.name: Ibra Rebate

rules.note: cost-plus must add up. The derived column makes this structurally true; the rule makes a client that posts its own sellingPriceMinor fail loudly instead of silently.
THE structural-integrity rule: the bank cannot sell what it does not own, and a zero-length ownership window is the commonest real defect. Strict < , not <=.
undisclosed cost makes it a Musawamah sale, not a Murabaha
the schedule may not total anything other than the fixed price
a price that moves after signing is interest wearing a sale's clothes. This is the rule that distinguishes the two.
no late-payment amount reaches income from this domain. The ledger-level proof is ISB-LPC-03 in Late Payment Charity Handling.
flag not reject: a genuine reimbursement of a customer who paid the supplier first exists, but it must be reviewed every time.
a pre-agreed rebate formula reintroduces the time value of money; permitted by some regulators (BNM) and not by others
the wa'd must be a separate instrument; two contracts in one is the defect
a build-time schema assertion. A Murabaha has an amount, never a rate. This one line is what stops the 49th domain reintroducing interest by a new name.

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: False for the CUSTOMER-facing receivable: once the sale executes the bank holds a fixed debt, not an equity stake. But the bank genuinely bears asset risk between bankOwnershipAcquiredAt and saleContractSignedAt, and that window is what makes the contract a sale rather than a loan. ISB-MRB-02 enforces that the window is non-empty; it cannot assert that the risk was economically real.

rules.note: a sale back to the original seller is bay' al-'inah, not tawarruq. This is the single most important rule in the domain.
the bank must own the commodity before it sells it on - the same ownership rule as Murabaha, applied per leg
generated as a window predicate over the child table; three legs stamped at the same instant are one netted entry wearing three names
the same commodity must move through every leg; a differing quantity means the legs are notional
OIC Fiqh Academy Resolution 179 (19/17) vs AAOIFI SS 30 is a genuine disagreement. The code flags and records; it does not decide.

DOWNGRADED TO A GENERATE-TIME COMMENT, NOT A LIVE RULE: see uncertain[]. The enum already excludes gold and silver, but 'ribawi commodity' is a juristic classification I cannot derive from a type code, so no runtime assert is honest here.
required, not optional, on the most contested structure in the estate
tawarruq is where a benchmark rate most often leaks in, because the markup is usually priced off one. Pricing INPUTS live in the product-pricing domain; the contract carries an amount.

standards.ref: International Islamic Fiqh Academy Resolution 179 (19/17), 17th session, 2009
standards.title: Tawarruq: organised and reverse tawarruq
Murabaha and Other Deferred Payment Sales

contested: The whole domain. Organised tawarruq is held impermissible by the OIC Fiqh Academy (Res. 179) and permissible in a constrained form by AAOIFI SS 30. No engineering choice resolves that; the catalog records the position taken and who approved it.
customerAppointedBankAsSellingAgent = true collapses the customer's possession to a bookkeeping entry.
uncertain: ISB-TWQ-09 is NOT a working rule. 'Ribawi commodity' is a juristic classification, not a data attribute; I can exclude gold and silver from an enum but I cannot mechanically decide whether some other commodity is ribawi. Left as a generate-time comment and reported as a gap.
I could not model the platform/broker cost split inside cashProceedsMinor well enough to assert that the customer was not charged a hidden spread. It needs a fee breakdown this domain does not own.
OIC Resolution 179's number and session are cited from the research record; I did not read the resolution text.

rules.note: determinate subject matter and delivery date are validity conditions; without them the contract is void for gharar, not merely incomplete
flag not reject: paying ahead of certified work is a credit decision, not a Shariah breach, but it is the pattern that turns an Istisna into an unsecured advance
the price may move only because the specification moved, and only with the document to prove it
in a parallel Istisna the bank is seller to the customer and buyer from the contractor; it must own the work in progress or it is selling what it does not have

rules.assert: priceDisclosureBasis == 'CostPlus' implies (isSet(estimatedCostMinor) && isSet(markupMinor) && totalIstisnaPriceMinor == estimatedCostMinor + markupMinor)

rules.note: khiyar al-ru'yah is a real right; exercising it must be recorded, because an undocumented rejection is how a bank walks away from its ownership risk
construction finance is where capitalised interest normally lives; there is no such field here

events.trigger: control record created at stage Specified

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: The bank bears genuine construction and delivery risk from Commissioned to Accepted - real, not nominal, and the reason Istisna is less contested than tawarruq. After acceptance it holds a receivable. capitalAtRisk is false in the DEPOSIT sense (no customer money is at risk here) but the bank's own capital is exposed during construction; the single boolean in DESIGN.md 8 cannot express both, so this note carries the difference.

standards.title: Default in Payment by a Debtor

contested: latePerformancePolicy = LiquidatedDamagesToCustomer: a liquidated-damages clause against the contractor is generally accepted as a price adjustment, but the boundary with a prohibited penalty is a board question.
paymentStructure = AdvanceFull makes the contract economically close to a Salam, which has stricter conditions.
uncertain: I modelled latePerformancePolicy (contractor delivers late) and latePaymentPolicy (customer pays late) as two separate fields because conflating them is a real and common modelling error. I am not certain the four latePerformancePolicy values are each individually permissible.

Percentage-of-completion revenue recognition under FAS 10 is an accounting concern this control record exposes (milestone values) but does not compute; whether that belongs here or in AAOIFI Financial Accounting is unresolved.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Shortfall Remediation
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined

rules.note: full prepayment is a validity condition of Salam. A deferred price on both sides is a prohibited sale of debt for debt.
deferred delivery is the essence of the contract; same-day delivery makes it an ordinary spot sale
the two Salams must stand alone; linking them makes each conditional on an uncertain event
on non-delivery the bank recovers its capital, never more. Any excess is riba, whatever it is called.
a generate-time check on the enum itself: Gold, Silver and Currency must not be addable as commodityType values without a board decision, because Salam over them is bay' al-sarf
substituting the subject matter is accepted by some boards for equivalent fungibles and rejected by others
the bank's return in a Salam is the price discount to expected spot, embedded in salamCapitalMinor. There is no rate to carry.

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: True, and genuinely so: the bank pays 100% up front against a future delivery and bears full counterparty and crop/production risk with no permitted compensation for delay. This is the one sale-based domain in the area where the bank's capital is unambiguously exposed.

standards.title: Salam and Parallel Salam
standards.appliesTo: full prepayment, determinate subject, parallel independence

standards.title: Salam and Parallel Salam
standards.appliesTo: measurement of Salam receivables and inventory

contested: substitutionAllowed = true.
shortfallRemedy = PurchaseInMarketAtSellerCost: charging the seller the market cost of covering looks like compensation for delay, which is the thing Salam may not have.
uncertain: Whether a Salam price may be below market by a margin that functions as a financing return is an economic-substance question. The data model records the price; it cannot judge it.

I excluded gold/silver/currency from the enum and wrote ISB-SLM-06 as a generate-time guard on the enum, which is weaker than a runtime rule. A board may also consider other commodities ribawi (e.g. staple foods by measure); I did not model that and it is a gap.

rules.note: no downstream sale may be executed until this stage is reached. The cross-service half of that sentence is enforced by ISB-MRB-02 in the Murabaha domain, which holds both timestamps; THIS service cannot see the other row.

fields.description: exact ratio, derived from the unit counts. No percentage column exists anywhere in this domain.

fields.name: baseMarketRentMinor
fields.description: market rent for the WHOLE property per period. The customer pays this scaled to the bank's current units - rent for the bank's share only.

fields.name: unitPurchaseBasis
fields.description: AgreedScheduleAtInception is the market norm and is contested: a pre-agreed buy-back price guarantees the bank's capital, which a partner may not do

fields.description: must be ProRataByShare - a partner bears its share of loss. Holds the wrong value so ISB-DMS-04 can reject it.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Unit Purchase
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined. Each row is a real sale of a real co-ownership share, which is why it carries its own price basis and its own title update - not an instalment number.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Rental Schedule
behaviourQualifiers.note: the rent FALLS as the bank's units fall, by exact integer arithmetic with a stated rounding direction (floor, i.e. in the customer's favour). A rental that does not fall with the bank's share is rent on a share the bank no longer owns.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Disposal
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined. The derivation order matters: the bank's share is floored and the customer takes the residual, so the two always sum to netProceedsMinor exactly and no minor unit is lost or invented.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Late Payment Charge
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined

rules.assert: bankCurrentUnits + customerCurrentUnits == totalUnits && bankInitialUnits + customerInitialUnits == totalUnits
rules.note: the co-ownership invariant. Everything else in this domain is derived from it.
THE rule of the domain: the customer pays rent for the bank's share and nothing more. Exact integer arithmetic with floor rounding; no float, no tolerance window.
a partner bears loss in proportion to capital. A customer bearing the whole loss on a jointly owned property was never a partner.

AgreedScheduleAtInception is the market norm and is contested, because a pre-agreed buy-back price guarantees the bank's capital and removes the price risk a partner is supposed to carry. Flagged with the SSB reference, not silently permitted and not blocked.
including on a LOSS: if netProceeds are below the capital contributed, the shortfall still splits by share
a unit purchase is a sale of a share, not a principal repayment. Diminishing Musharakah implemented as an amortisation table with a rent label is the defect this whole domain exists to avoid.

shariah.contractSubType: Musharakah Mutanaqisah (diminishing), with an Ijara leg over the bank's share
shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: True: the bank is a co-owner. If the property falls in value the bank's units fall with it (ISB-DMS-08), and if usufruct fails its rent stops. This is the only financing domain in my area where the bank's exposure is equity rather than receivable - which is also why unitPurchaseBasis matters so much: AgreedScheduleAtInception quietly converts it back into a receivable.

profit may be shared by agreement; loss follows capital, always. This is the clearest bright line in partnership fiqh and the one a developer is most likely to smooth over.

a pre-agreed exit price makes the bank's capital certain and the partnership nominal

a permissible contract over a prohibited activity is still prohibited

behaviourQualifiers.note: coined

a guaranteed Mudarabah is a loan. This is the bright line of the contract.
the mudarib loses its effort, not its money - unless negligence or a breach of restrictions is ESTABLISHED on the record with evidence
structurally true because rabbUlMalAmountMinor is the residual, and asserted anyway so a client posting its own numbers fails loudly

rules.assert: capitalImpairmentMinor > 0 implies sum(profitDistribution[] where isOnAccount == false -> distributableProfitMinor) == 0
rules.note: profit is the excess over capital; capital must be made whole before any profit exists to share
a management fee on top of a profit share is contested: the profit share IS the mudarib's compensation. Flagged, with the SSB reference required to stand behind it.
tandid hukmi is standard practice for periodic profit on investment accounts and still needs a board position on this product
the single most important build-time assertion in the area: a Mudarabah schema with a minimum-return column is not a Mudarabah, and no runtime rule can undo a column that exists

Whether a third party (not the mudarib) may guarantee the capital.

the strictest schema assertion in the area, and the only one that bans the word 'profit' outright. A Qard Hassan record that can hold a return is already wrong, whatever the value in it.

an over-recovery on a benevolent loan is not an accounting rounding issue, it is the prohibited increase

behaviourQualifiers.note: coined. ta'widh must equal the sum of these evidenced rows (ISB-LPC-04), which is what stops it being a rate on the overdue balance wearing a compensation label. lossType FundingCost is itself contested, because the 'cost of funds' on a delayed payment is close to the thing being prohibited.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Ledger Posting
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined, append-only, and the audit trail that answers the only question that matters: where did the money go. Signed, because a reversal is a negative posting and not a deletion.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Charity Disbursement
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined. The bank may not direct this to a cause that benefits it, which is a governance control this record can evidence but not enforce.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Waiver
behaviourQualifiers.note: coined

rules.note: the two components are different things with different destinations, so the total must decompose exactly
the central rule of the domain, and the enum has only one value so the generated CHECK constraint enforces it at the database as well

THE ledger-level proof. The destination field is a statement of intent; the GL class is where the money actually went, and both are checked. An auditor can read this rule and the Ledger Posting rows and verify the claim without trusting the application.
ta'widh is compensation for documented loss, so it equals the documented loss. Any formula over the overdue amount fails this.
and ISB-LPC-06 flags it as well, because a permitted practice in one jurisdiction is a breach in another and the code must not quietly pick a side
a flag, never a block: BNM permits ta'widh up to actual loss as income in Malaysia; AAOIFI's position is stricter. The estate records the position and who authorised it.
a debtor unable to pay is granted time. Charging hardship is the practice the prohibition exists to prevent.
the penalty element requires a finding that the default was wilful; assessing nobody and charging everybody is the default implementation and it is wrong
every penalty minor unit assessed must leave the bank. Where tawidhDestination is also CharityPool, ISB-LPC-10 adds that component.
split from ISB-LPC-09 rather than written with a conditional expression, to keep the grammar free of ternaries
a charge assessed before the payment was late is not a late-payment charge
a per-diem rate on an overdue balance IS default interest, whatever the column is called. There is no rate in this schema - only evidenced amounts.

a generate-time assertion on the emitted repository: this control record is append-only, so the template must not generate a delete method or a DELETE statement for this table. DESIGN.md 5.8 - a DELETE destroying a compliance record is a correctness bug.

events.name: shariah.compliance.flagged
events.trigger: any flag rule fires, notably ISB-LPC-06

shariah.contractTypeNote: not a contract: a compliance procedure attached to the other eleven. contractType is 'None' rather than a borrowed value, because labelling it Murabaha or Ijara would make the catalog claim a contract that does not exist here.
shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: No capital is at risk. The money handled here is money the bank must NOT keep.
shariah.reviewStatus: UNREVIEWED - requires named Shariah board sign-off

standards.title: Default in Payment by a Debtor (Procrastinating Debtor)
standards.appliesTo: the ta'widh / gharamah distinction, forbearance for hardship

standards.title: Compensation for late payment of financial obligations
standards.appliesTo: jurisdiction = MY: the basis on which tawidhDestination may be BankIncome up to actual loss. Cited as issuer/regulator practice, NOT as a universal ruling.

contested: tawidhDestination = BankIncome: the single sharpest jurisdictional split in the whole estate.
actualLossEvidence.lossType = FundingCost: treating the cost of funds over the delay as an actual loss is close to charging for time.
Whether gharamah may be charged at all, as opposed to the debt simply being enforced.
uncertain: The BNM reference is cited by name and subject from the research record; I did not read the policy document and have NOT cited a clause or a date. It must be verified before it appears in any customer-facing or regulator-facing artefact.

This service cannot verify that the referenced facility is genuinely overdue - that row lives in another service's schema. A charge raised against a current facility would pass every rule here. The source domain must raise the charge; a client calling this service directly can bypass that, and the estate has no mechanism that prevents it.
I modelled the destination as a per-entry field. Whether a bank may net charity-destined amounts across entries before disbursing, and over what period, is a governance question I could not resolve.
